Deprecation Notice:
The Marketing Version 202601 (Marketing January 2026) will be sunset on January 15, 2027. We recommend that you migrate to the latest versioned APIs to avoid disruptions. For information on all the supported versions, refer to the migrations documentation.
If you haven’t yet migrated and have questions, submit a request on the LinkedIn Developer Support Portal.
Boost lets a member or a Company Page turn an existing, eligible post into a sponsored ad without leaving the native post-boosting flow. The Boost APIs support two separate identity contexts:

Member Boost - Boosts a post owned by the authenticated member. See Member Post Boost.
Company Page Boost - Boosts a post on behalf of an organization the authenticated member can manage. See Organization Post Boost.

Each context exposes a parallel set of REST.li actions and finders. Member Boost endpoints are prefixed member (for example, memberBoostInit) and Company Page Boost endpoints are prefixed organization (for example, organizationBoostInit).
The shared targeting and saved-audience resource uses account ownership rather than a member or organization path prefix.
Your developer application must be approved for the Advertising API product for the relevant Boost permissions to call these endpoints.
Note

For fetching member posts, your application must have created the posts with the w_member_social permission and saved their post IDs from the response. Fetching member posts is restricted with the r_member_social permission under the "Member Posts Management API" product, which has closed access.

Blocks.Text: A typical Boost integration calls the following endpoints in sequence for a given post:

Status - Call memberBoostStatus or organizationBoostStatus to confirm the post is eligible to be boosted and to learn why it is ineligible if not.
Init - Call memberBoostInit or organizationBoostInit to resolve or create the sponsored account and billing configuration that will fund the boost.
Hydrate - Call memberBoostHydrate or organizationBoostHydrate to preview targeting, forecast, and pricing for a hypothetical budget and objective before committing.
Post - Call memberBoostPost or organizationBoostPost to create the sponsored campaign group, campaign, and creative that make up the boost.
Analytics - Call boostAnalytics (see Boost Analytics) to retrieve performance metrics for member and organization posts that have already been boosted.
Note
Applications must be authorized and authenticated before they can fetch data from LinkedIn or get access to LinkedIn member data. To learn more about the OAuth flows, see Authentication.
Note

The advertiser doesn't need a payment method on file before you start. Init returns billingConfigured: false when billing setup is needed. Redirect the advertiser to https://www.linkedin.com/campaignmanager/boost/billing/{account_id}?origin=partner, replacing {account_id} with the numeric ID from the account URN that init returned. After the advertiser finishes billing setup, call init again and continue only when it returns billingConfigured: true.
The user is the authenticated member boosting their own post.

Authenticate. Obtain a 3-legged OAuth token for the member with r_member_boost and rw_member_boost.
Check eligibility. GET /rest/memberBoostStatus?q=boostStatus&targetPosts=List({encodedPostUrn}).
Initialize the boost. POST /rest/memberBoostInit?action=init. If the response returns billingConfigured: false, redirect the member to the billing setup page, then call init again before continuing.
Make the first hydrate call to get the suggested configuration. POST /rest/memberBoostHydrate?action=hydrate.

Use the values from the init response in this first request.
Don't set totalBudget in the first hydrate request.
After the first hydrate call returns, the member can change only the objective, run schedule, and budget. Call hydrate each time one of these changes to get the latest forecast. Pass the suggested targetingCriteria into each later hydrate call, and stay within the boost limits (minimum spend) returned by the first hydrate call.


Create and launch the boost. POST /rest/memberBoostPost?action=post. Set callToActionLabel.value and callToActionTarget only when the goal is LEAD_GENERATION.
Retrieve analytics. GET /rest/boostAnalytics?q=boostAnalytics&targetPosts=List({postUrn}).
Manage the ad. Use this flow when a member wants to review or stop a boost they already started:

Find the boost. Call GET /rest/memberBoostStatus for the post. If the post has a current or past boost, the status is CURRENTLY_BOOSTED, IN_REVIEW, SCHEDULED, or PREVIOUSLY_BOOSTED, and the response includes the campaign URN and account URN for that boost. You need both URNs for the next steps.
Load the boost details. Pass the campaign URN and account URN to POST /rest/memberBoostInit?action=init. The response contains the campaign's objective and run schedule, so you can show the member those settings.
End the boost. When the member confirms they want to stop the boost, call DELETE /rest/memberBoostCampaign/{campaignId}?account={encodedAccountUrn} using the numeric campaign ID and URL-encoded account URN.
Note

memberBoostPost (at creation) and memberBoostInit also return the campaign and account URNs, so you can reuse them from an earlier step. memberBoostStatus is the most reliable way to look them up for any post.
The user is a Company Page admin boosting a page post.

Authenticate. Obtain a 3-legged OAuth token for the page admin with r_organization_boost and rw_organization_boost.
Check eligibility. GET /rest/organizationBoostStatus?q=boostStatus&organization={organizationUrn}&targetPosts=List({encodedPostUrn}).
Initialize the boost. POST /rest/organizationBoostInit?action=init. If the response returns billingConfigured: false, redirect the admin to the billing setup page, then call init again before continuing.
Make the first hydrate call to get the suggested configuration. POST /rest/organizationBoostHydrate?action=hydrate.

Use the values from the init response in this first request.
Don't set totalBudget in the first hydrate request.
After the first hydrate call returns, the admin can change only the objective, run schedule, and budget. Call hydrate each time one of these changes. Pass the suggested targetingCriteria into each later hydrate call, and stay within the boost limits (minimum spend) returned by the first hydrate call.


Create and launch the boost. POST /rest/organizationBoostPost?action=post. Set callToActionLabel.value and callToActionTarget only when the goal is LEAD_GENERATION.
Retrieve analytics. GET /rest/boostAnalytics?q=boostAnalytics&targetPosts=List({postUrn})&organization={encodedOrganizationUrn}.
Manage the ad. Follow the same steps as the member flow, using the organization endpoints (organizationBoostStatus, organizationBoostInit, and organizationBoostCampaign).

Authenticate with rw_member_boost for Member Boost or rw_organization_boost for Company Page Boost. The end-to-end creation workflow requires write permission; read-only scopes aren't sufficient for Init, Hydrate, or Post.
Check eligibility with GET /rest/memberBoostStatus?q=boostStatus&targetPosts=List({encodedPostUrn}), or the organization equivalent GET /rest/organizationBoostStatus?q=boostStatus&organization={organizationUrn}&targetPosts=List({encodedPostUrn}) with the sponsoring organization.
Initialize with POST /rest/memberBoostInit?action=init or POST /rest/organizationBoostInit?action=init. The organization action requires organization in its body. Optionally provide a locale with language and country/region.
If billingConfigured is false, open the returned billingUrl without rebuilding it or removing query parameters. After setup, call Init again and continue only when billing is configured. Your application never collects payment details.
Use Init's targetingEntities to discover targeting options, or select an account-owned saved audience.
Preview with POST /rest/memberBoostHydrate?action=hydrate or the organization equivalent POST /rest/organizationBoostHydrate?action=hydrate. Omit totalBudget on the first preview to obtain suggestions. Preview changes to audience, objective, schedule, or budget before creating the boost.
Collect a political declaration when Hydrate returns politicalDeclarationRequired: true. An absent flag isn't a confirmed false; don't treat it as permission to skip an otherwise required declaration. For EU targeting, display the mandatory consent using the required wording and presentation, clearly presented and checked by default before submitting or activating the boost. Sending NOT_POLITICAL alone doesn't satisfy the consent requirement. LinkedIn prohibits political advertising.
Create with POST /rest/memberBoostPost?action=post or the organization equivalent POST /rest/organizationBoostPost?action=post. Supply previewed targeting and, when required, politicalIntent: {"value":"NOT_POLITICAL"}. Use call-to-action fields only for LEAD_GENERATION goal (callToActionLabel.value and callToActionTarget).
Retrieve analytics with GET /rest/boostAnalytics?q=boostAnalytics&targetPosts=List({postUrn}). Include organization for Company Page analytics.
Manage the boost using the returned account and campaign: GET details, POST a partial update to targeting or political declaration, or DELETE after user confirmation.
Member Boost still rejects a start on a future UTC day. Company Page Boost supports future starts. Both require start and end timestamps covering at least two UTC calendar days, counted inclusively.

Blocks.Text: The Boost button on the Page posts tab reflects the status returned by organizationBoostStatus. A disabled button indicates the post can't be boosted.

The Audience dropdown lets the advertiser select a suggested or saved audience. Retrieve saved audiences with GET /rest/boostTargetingCriteria?q=account&account={encodedAccountUrn}, then pass the selected targeting criteria to the hydrate endpoint to refresh the preview.

Selecting Create audience opens the targeting editor, where the advertiser can name an audience and choose attributes to include or exclude. Use Init's targetingEntities to populate the targeting controls, and save the audience with POST /rest/boostTargetingCriteria. See Boost targeting and saved audiences for discovery, creation, and editing details.

Selecting Boost opens the boost creation flow. Selecting a goal calls the init endpoint, changing the audience, budget, or schedule calls the hydrate endpoint to refresh the preview, and selecting Boost calls the post endpoint.
After a post is boosted, the Boost tab on the post analytics page shows the performance data returned by boostAnalytics.
